title: A preserved-work stop is never observed under host load
description:
`TestAStoppedAttemptSPreservedWorkReachesTheNextAttempt` (internal/reconcile, prior_snapshots_test.go:94) failed in the e9n attempt-8 integrated gate after 595.97s:

    the run's feed never said a1's wall clock fired:
    the stop the snapshot preserves was never observed

The same commit (46caa836a30c) passes the whole reconcile package on a quiet host: ok 499.216s. It failed only when the package took 1363s instead of its ~180s quiet baseline.

Per the standing 'flaky = bug' policy this is a defect, not load noise. The test waits for a wall_clock_fired feed line; under contention it gives up before the line arrives. Either the wall clock genuinely does not fire when the host is busy — which would be a production bug, since a wall clock that only fires on an idle machine is not a bound — or the test waits on a derived signal with its own deadline instead of on the observable. Determine which before fixing, and do not widen the timeout.

Sibling of e4u; both stopped the epic-dha Phase 5 run at 12:47 on failures that do not reproduce. Root cause of the exposure is miu.
acceptance_criteria: The test passes deterministically under injected contention, with the fix naming whether the wall clock or the test's wait was at fault, proven without widening a timeout
